v1.label: L-desk v1: freestanding, drawers by the chaise
v1._note: Bedroom 2 study, L-shaped (client 2026-11-18, IKEA 'desk hack' reference). IKEA EKBACKEN brown walnut effect worktops, 28 thick, full 635 deep. West run under W1: 246 length (804.429.85, $179) cut to 2100, y 8.05-10.15, into the north-west corner; it stops 64 short of the swing of the robe's west door (656 wide, reaches y 10.214 opened flat to the wall). North run: 186 length (704.429.81, $149) cut to 1805, x 2.25-4.055, butted against the west run's front edge with three worktop connector bolts (routed under, 28 minimum thickness) plus biscuits. Supports: two EKET 2-drawer cabinets 70x35x35 (606.167.50) stacked at the far end of each run, standing on the floor without feet (fronts 10 behind the worktop edge); 42x19 cleats screwed to the west and north walls; one ADILS leg, black, 70 cm (002.179.76, $5) under the inside corner, which is otherwise 635 out from both walls with nothing under it (IKEA: legs no more than 80 cm apart where the worktop overhangs more than 25 cm). Top 728, leg room (floor to underside) 700, the ADILS's exact length. Knee space: 755 wide under the window (corner leg to drawers, y 8.685-9.44), 1.095 along the north wall (x 2.96-4.055). Without EKET feet so the top clears W1's architraves (~740). BILLY bookcase 80x28x202 (606.183.96) + height extension 80x28x35 (105.086.68), 237 high, brown walnut effect, at the east end of the north wall (x 1.43-2.23), the north run stopping 20 short of it; one shelf set level with the desk top UPDATE 2026-11-18 (client): the north run's EKET stack is removed (an ADILS leg under its end instead) and a King Living 1977 Sofa Chaise (kingliving.com.au 1977-chaise-v3, 860 W x 1480 D x 710 H, from $1,303, Leura S boucle to match the lounge couch) stands along the east wall between the BILLY and the door: x 1.43-2.29, y 8.37-9.85, back cushion at the door (south) end so you sit facing the desk and window. Fit: 1.557 between the BILLY's front (y 8.348) and the door's architrave (y 9.905), so 1.48 leaves ~20 at the bookcase and ~55 at the architrave. The north run now ends at x 2.32 (cut 1735 from the 186), 30 clear of the chaise. Renovated: the door is rehung on its south jamb and opens toward the robe, away from the chaise; the light switch (centre 1.05, y ~9.86) is above the 710 back. Current house: check which jamb the door hangs on; hinged on the north jamb its 800 leaf would sweep to y ~9.18 and hit the chaise. Clear floor from the chaise to the west run's front edge: 1.77 UPDATE 2 (client 2026-11-18): BILLY removed. The chaise moves into the north-east corner, back cushion against the north wall and the seat (legs) running toward the robes: x 1.43-2.29, y 8.07-9.55; 355 clear of the door's architrave (y 9.905). The north desk run still ends at x 2.32, 30 clear of the chaise's side UPDATE 3 (client 2026-11-18): the EKET drawer stack moves from the south end of the window run to the east end of the north run, beside the chaise: x 2.33-3.03, fronts facing south at y 8.675 (40 clear of the chaise's side). The window run's south end now stands on an ADILS leg under its front corner and the west-wall cleat runs its full length. Knee space: 1.44 under the window (corner leg to end leg, y 8.685-10.12), ~1.0 along the north wall (x 3.03-4.055) UPDATE 4 (client 2026-11-18): FREESTANDING, nothing fixed to the walls, and no leg at the inside corner (knee space). Supports: the EKET stack at the north run's east end, plus seven IKEA ADILS legs, black, 70 cm (002.179.76, $5 each; 40 dia, adjustable foot, 50 kg max load each; OLOV was rejected at 13 kg), each centred 50 in from the edges (the two front legs 85 in, behind the steel angle): (1) the outer (north-west) corner against both walls, x 4.64 y 8.10; (2) west run back, mid, x 4.64 y 9.10; (3) and (4) west run south end, back x 4.64 / front x 4.14, y 10.10; (5) north run back, x 3.55 y 8.10, and (6) its front, x 3.55 y 8.60, 500 east of the inside corner and clear of the knee space at the window; (7) north run back behind the EKET stack, x 2.37 y 8.10 (the stack is 350 deep and the top 635). Inside corner: 40x40x3 steel angle (Bunnings) screwed under both front edges, from the south-end leg round the corner to the EKET stack, mitred and joined with a flat steel L-plate, plus the three worktop connector bolts and biscuits in the butt joint; this carries the corner between leg (6) and leg (4) instead of a leg there. Spans: west front edge 1.42 m from the corner to leg (4) on the steel angle; back edges <= 1.0 m between legs; north front 0.5 m cantilever from leg (6) to the corner. The L shape itself stops side-to-side racking; screw the EKET carcass to the worktop. If the corner still bounces when leaned on, add an ADILS at the corner as the fallback UPDATE 5 (client 2026-11-18): no front leg on the north run either (leg 6 removed) so the chair can roll freely around the inside of the L. Six ADILS remain: outer corner, window-run back mid, window-run south end back and front, north-run back (x 3.55, against the wall), north-run back behind the EKET stack. The whole front edge now hangs between the EKET stack (x 3.03) and the window run's south-end front leg (y 10.10), 2.45 m around the corner. So the front steel is upgraded from 40x40 angle to 50x25x2.0 steel RHS (rectangular hollow section), set 30 in from the front edge, welded into one L at the inside corner (a steel fabricator, or bolt through a heavy internal corner bracket), screwed up into both worktops every ~150. Closed section because, with no corner leg, the frame must resist twist as well as bending; open angle would let the corner drop. The worktops tie the frame back to the four back legs, which take the twist. Expect the inside corner to be the springiest point; it should feel solid for normal use (laptop, monitor, arms), not for sitting on UPDATE 6 (client 2026-11-18): the leg behind the EKET stack is dropped. Two EKETs stacked are 700, the same as an ADILS, so the leg was not about height: it carried the 275 of worktop behind the 350-deep stack. The stack now sits 40 back from the front edge (drawers_inset 0.04), which leaves 245 behind it, inside IKEA's 250 overhang limit, with the carcass screwed up into the worktop; the drawer fronts get a 40 shadow line. Five ADILS remain: outer corner, window-run back mid, window-run south end back and front, north-run back at x 3.55

No media shelf (client: nobody uses it). On feet the cabinets are 372 high (400 with the worktop), under W2's sill board (z 0.42) but not its architrave (z 0.39 up, at x 4.67-4.69), so every floor run stops at x 4.66. The usable wall runs from there to the hall doorway's architrave (x 0.995): 3.665. 3.5 m of cabinets fits (x 4.66-1.16), and with the worktop ends 3.556 (x 4.66-1.104, 109 clear of the architrave). The EKBACKEN comes 246 or 186 long by 635 deep: ripped to 380, the top needs 3.556 and the two ends 2 x ~0.37, 4.3 m in all, so two 246 lengths, with one join in the top (put it over a cabinet joint). Backs sit 18 off the wall against the 170 skirting; the worktop ends are scribed over it. A 75" TV standing on the worktop has its screen centre at ~0.95 (on the bare cabinets ~0.93), a little under seated eye height (~1.0-1.1). No open 70x35x35 exists in walnut, hence the door-off cabinet. 60 mm cable holes through the adjoining side panels and the backs; soundbar on top in front of the TV (needs to be under ~75 high to clear the screen on its stand). 'eWide3' (client 2026-11-18: devices hidden behind doors, holes drilled in the backs, no 35 cubes): three wide door cabinets, 2.1 m (y 12.792-14.892, 1.19 short of the north wall; four would be 2.8 m and end 0.49 from the hall doorway wall). TV centre y 13.84. eRec closed up (client 2026-11-18): the equipment bay gets its door back, so console and amp sit behind the south wide door with cable holes in the back
